content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P0 Alert: serving/runtime - sudden CPU spike on tokenizer pods in us-west-2, multiple OOM/killed events and pod evictions detected. Pager sent to @eric (oncall).

sam: @eric you up? we started getting 5xx spikes on /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings around 14:07 UTC. perf dashboards show tokenizer pods at 95-100% CPU, kubelet evicting.

eric (oncall): on it. I'm pulling logs and checking cluster autoscaler. doing a quick triage. can someone flag customer impact?

lina (support): seeing elevated errors for 3 customers (acct: acme, beta-app, marketing-ai). ACME reports high latency + some 503s. I've opened support tickets and attached request ids.

jen (infra): initial look - node flaps in nodepool-tokenize-1; kernel OOMs for container PID 21437. Heap/CPU steadily grew after a batch of long prompts (huge token counts) started routing to tokenizer replicas.

sam: here's a snippet from pod logs (tokenizer sidecar):

```
2026-03-15T14:06:58Z tokenizer_worker.py: process_batch size=128 token_count=8232 cpu=97%
2026-03-15T14:07:03Z tokenizer_worker.py: AllocError: cannot allocate memory for token buffer
2026-03-15T14:07:04Z kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 21437 (python) total-vm:650000kB, anon-rss:540000kB
2026-03-15T14:07:05Z kubelet: Pod "tokenizer-abcde-2" evicted due to node alloc pressure
```

eric (oncall): thanks. immediate plan: 1) put a soft rate-limit on tokenization-heavy endpoints; 2) scale tokenizer Deployment replicas + rotate pods off affected nodes; 3) cordon nodepool-tokenize-1 to stop new pods scheduling; 4) temporary rollback to smaller tokenizer model variant for hosted tier while we stabilize.

jen (infra): executing now - cordoning nodepool-tokenize-1, scaling tokenizer replicas from 5 -> 12 in us-west-2 to spread load. also bumping CPU requests on new pods to try and avoid OOM kill churn.

eric (oncall): running commands:

```
kubectl cordon node/nodepool-tokenize-1 -n redwood-prod
kubectl scale deployment/tokenizer --replicas=12 -n redwood-prod\kubectl get pods -n redwood-prod -o wide | grep tokenizer\kubectl describe pod tokenizer-abcde-2 -n redwood-prod
```

sam: pushed a throttling rule to the edge to cap tokenization input size to 4k tokens and to rate-limit requests with token_count>2k to 10 rps per org. (edge-rule id: ER-735).

lina (support): notifying impacted customers: ACME told they may see transient 503s and that we are mitigating; CS rep @raj on standby for escalation.

raj (cs): on it — will send targeted update to ACME and Beta-app once we confirm stabilization.

jen (infra): node cordoned. new tokenizer pods scheduled on healthy nodes. initial metrics show CPU for tokenizer pods dropping from 98% -> ~60% on new pods.

eric (oncall): monitoring logs for backpressure loop. quick check: are we batching too aggressively for large prompts? this looks like a tokenizer backlog where batch sizes multiplied token counts and blew past resource caps.

sam: yes, workload analysis shows bursty long-prompt traffic from a small set of customers that hit our continuous-batching window; batching parameters allowed huge groupings when prompt lengths are large. we should cap batch_size by total_token_budget.

eric (oncall): mitigation checklist (in-flight):
- edge token limit + rate limit (applied)
- cordon affected nodepool (done)
- scale replicas and schedule to healthy nodes (done)
- restart evicted pods to get new resource requests (in progress)
- temporary model variant fallback for hosted tier (wip)
- add emergency alert to disable continuous-batching if CPU>85% for >2m (wip)

jen (infra): I've restarted the tokenizer pods with updated resources and QoS (guaranteed when possible). also created a k8s eviction-resistant policy for tokenizer to prioritize graceful shutdowns.

eric (oncall): preliminary customer impact assessment: ~0.8% of total hosted requests returned 503/504 during the 14:06-14:20 window. ACME experienced 18 minutes of elevated latency and ~120 failed calls. billing impact minimal; SLA noise likely.

lina (support): tickets updated with timeline and mitigation steps. asking for post-incident follow-up plan from infra/eng.

sam: root cause (candidate): no hard cap on continuous-batching total token budget -> long prompts from a few orgs triggered excessive batch-level memory use causing CPU saturation and OOM kills.

eric (oncall): next actions (owner):
- infra/eng (jen + sam): implement token-budget-aware batching (limit batch token budget to 8k total) and enforce per-request token size limit at router (eta: 48h)
- infra (jen): add autoscaler rule to spin up additional tokenizer nodes when tokenizer CPU >70% for 1m (eta: 24h)
- devex (sam): surface consumer docs + warnings for large prompts and provide best-practice sample code (eta: 72h)
- run a chaos test to ensure graceful degradation under batch-heavy workloads (owner: eng-runtime, eta: 1 week)

eric (oncall): handing off to daytime oncall @sam (primary) and @jen (infra follow). I'll leave the incident channel open; i'll rotate to watch window for one hour then mark acknowledged.

sam: acknowledged handoff — I'll own the postmortem and follow-ups. will capture timeline and add remediation tickets.

jen (infra): monitoring shows error rate trending down, new pods stable. will keep nodes cordoned for 30m and then slowly uncordon after validation.

eric (oncall): status update to execs and SRE on-call: sending short note.

incident-bot: Incident 2026-03-15T14:07: P0 resolved to mitigation state. follow-ups created: TICKET-4182 (batching hard cap), TICKET-4183 (autoscaler rule), TICKET-4184 (router token limit), TICKET-4185 (postmortem draft).

lina (support): marking affected customer tickets as 'waiting for engineering follow-up'.

raj (cs): sent customer note to ACME & Beta-app summarizing impact and short-term fix. will wait for postmortem for detailed RCA before a full account review.

sam: postmortem plan: include traffic traces of offending requests, batch-size histograms, kubelet eviction events, and suggested config defaults. assigning owners for remediation PRs.

jen (infra): uncordoning nodepool-tokenize-1 at 14:48 UTC after monitoring window.

eric (oncall): closing active pager; will mark incident status as "mitigated - monitoring". final notes: consider adding token-size heuristics to routing policy so costlier requests are isolated.

sam: thanks everyone. I'll file the postmortem and link it here when ready. :thumbsup:

(End of thread)
